blockers.appliesTo: PTCB-V25-B2 / CLAUDE-V25-S2 — answered by restoring linux-pathless; the restored bind cannot be satisfied
blockers.title: measuredBootBind equates a PCR-4 EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION event digest with a flat file sha-256, which are different preimages, so the equality can never hold and every Linux profile remains unqualifiable
blockers.whatIsGenuinelyBetter: I want to be precise about how much ground this covers, because it is a lot. The v24 defect was that IMA runtime file measurement proves a file was read, not that it is executing. measuredBootBind replaces that with an actual attestation ceremony: the TCG2 event log is retained exactly; a TPM2_Quote is taken over PCR 4 with a nonce fixed to sha-256 of runIdentity concatenated with observedAt, which is genuine boot-and-run freshness rather than the v24 list-existence check; the AK signature must verify against a certificate-store TCB member, which anchors trust inside the contract's own taxonomy instead of an unnamed root; and pcrMatch requires the quoted PCR 4 to equal an event-log reconstruction that includes kernelEvent, which is the correct replay discipline and was entirely absent at v24. unavailableRefuses is comprehensive and fails closed on no TPM, no log, no unique event, quote failure or nonce mismatch, and it explicitly keeps Linux in D-002 slice 1 rather than minting a deferral. Structurally this is the ceremony Codex B2 and I asked for. The defect is one link inside it.
blockers.theDefect: equality reads 'kernelEvent digest (sha-256) MUST equal authenticatedKernelMember.sha256', where authenticatedKernelMember is a '{relativePath, sha256}' member of the authenticated package payload and every other sha256 in this contract is a flat digest of exact file bytes. But kernelEvent is specified as 'the unique TCG event whose eventType is EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION'. Under the TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile, the digest carried by that event type is the PE/COFF image digest computed the Authenticode way when firmware loads the image: the hash is taken over the PE image with the optional-header CheckSum field, the Certificate Table data directory entry, and the attribute certificate table region excluded and the remaining ranges hashed in a defined order. It is a sha-256 in algorithm but not a sha-256 of the file's bytes. For any real kernel EFI binary the two values differ, so the equality is unsatisfiable — and it is unsatisfiable in the safe direction, meaning the profile refuses rather than admitting bad bytes, but it refuses always.
blockers.exhaustivenessEvidence: I searched the whole 149517-byte artifact for any handling of this distinction: 'Authenticode' 0 occurrences, 'PE/COFF' 0, 'PECOFF' 0, 'PE image' 0, 'image hash' 0. There is exactly 1 occurrence of 'EV_EFI', in the kernelEvent clause itself. Nothing anywhere defines a PE image-digest computation, and nothing requires the package member to be reduced to such a digest before comparison.
blockers.compoundingFacet: The same clause also assumes a boot path in which firmware itself loads the kernel as a UEFI boot services application. That happens on EFI-stub direct boot; it does not happen on the common bootloader path, where the loader loads the kernel through its own loader rather than firmware LoadImage and measures it into a different PCR, leaving no EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION event whose digest is the kernel at all. The contract quotes only PCR 4 and enumerates only that one event type, with 0 occurrences of any other PCR index anywhere in the artifact. On its own this facet would be defensible as a disclosed narrowing, since unavailableRefuses says machines without a unique kernel event fail qualification. Combined with the preimage mismatch it removes the remaining case, so no configuration qualifies.
blockers.failureScenario: A fully compliant machine: UEFI with TPM 2.0, Secure Boot on, kernel booted directly as an EFI-stub PE image, kernel package installed from the publisher's signed repository. Firmware measures the kernel PE image into PCR 4 as EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION with the Authenticode image digest D_pe. The verifier retains the TCG2 log, takes a TPM2_Quote over PCR 4 with the required nonce, verifies the AK against a certificate-store TCB member, and replays the log to match the quoted PCR — every one of those steps passes. It then computes authenticatedKernelMember as the unique payload member whose sha256 equals the kernel event digest. No such member exists, because every member's sha256 is a flat file digest and D_pe is not one. 'Zero or more than one refuses.' The profile refuses on a machine that satisfies every security property the ceremony was designed to prove. Since OS ABI MUST use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED and on Linux that tag now routes to measuredBootBind, no Linux OS ABI entry can ever be represented, and pathlessClasses.rule forbids representing it any other way. That is PTCB-V25-B2's condition — 'every Linux profile unqualifiable' — reproduced through a specified-but-unsatisfiable bind instead of a withdrawal, while the contract carries standing LIVE and linuxStanding presents TPM absence as the only failure mode.
blockers.whyThisIsABlocker: Codex rated the identical condition a blocker at v25 and the dispatch forbids removing Linux from D-002 slice 1, so the contract cannot fall back on withdrawal or deferral. A profile marked LIVE whose central equality cannot be satisfied on any machine is not a weaker version of the repair; it is the same defect wearing the ceremony's clothes, and it is the third generation in which the Linux executing-kernel bind has been asserted rather than delivered.
blockers.requiredRepair: Fix the preimage, not the ceremony, which is otherwise sound. Either (1) define the PE/COFF image-digest computation normatively — naming the excluded CheckSum field, the Certificate Table directory entry and the attribute certificate region, and the hashing order — and require the authenticated payload member to be reduced to that image digest before comparison, retaining both the member's flat sha256 and its computed image digest; or (2) bind through a measurement whose preimage is the file bytes, naming the event type and PCR that actually carries it on the boot paths in scope, and requiring equality to the member's flat sha256. In either case, state which boot configurations are in scope and which refuse, so the narrowing is disclosed rather than emergent, and keep the quote, nonce, AK-anchoring, replay and fail-closed rules exactly as they are — they are correct.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V25-B1 — RPM materialization begins from an undefined blob and does not preserve one file identity across hash, checksig and extraction
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, and it takes the branch Codex preferred. preferredApi holds a single librpm descriptor from rpmReadPackageFile across all three stages, with 'lseek to 0 between stages. Do not close and reopen', the digest taken as sha-256 of a pread of the entire descriptor and required to equal authenticityCore.payload.digest, verification via rpmVerifySignatures on that same descriptor, and extraction by rpmfi walk of that same header. The CLI fallback is properly hardened for the case where the descriptor path is not used: mkdirat a run-owned 0700 directory owned by observerProcessIdentity, a filename restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._+-]+, openat with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC at 0600, write-once plus fsync, an identityRecord of {dev, ino, size, sha256} from fstat, and — the element Codex specifically demanded — fstatat O_NOFOLLOW revalidation of that same identity after checksig AND again after extraction, with mismatch refusing. materializedFileIdentity is retained as closed evidence. selectionKey now also binds the NEVRA to the signed core: 'That NEVRA MUST equal authenticityCore.payload.name plus EVR.'

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V25-S1 second half — EXTERNAL directory derivation undefined

limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed the six claimed repairs, the restored measured-boot surface, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness. CLAUDE-V26-B1 rests on the documented semantics of EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION in the TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile and the PE image-digest definition it references, not on execution against live firmware; a successor that disputes it should do so on those semantics, and the repair I specify does not require conceding the point, since defining the image-digest computation makes the equality correct under either reading.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 5128f401... and 0444 at both ends, HEAD steady, 33/33 chain pins reproduce, both frozen v25 verdicts reproduce with no replacement, and the v25-to-v26 diff is 43 paths with zero off-roster. Five repairs are made cleanly. The RPM branch now holds one librpm descriptor across digest, verify and extract, with a hardened openat/O_NOFOLLOW fallback that revalidates {dev, ino, size, sha256} after both checksig and extraction — the descriptor-capable branch Codex preferred. Manifest hash uniqueness is removed at both sites with an explicit supersession clause, so duplicate member digests including empty files are lawful. The EXTERNAL derivation is now exact with no full-path fallback. rpmHeaderIdentity is gated to rpm-checksig, forbidden on apt-secure, and bound to the query output, the NEVRA and the event token. And Linux is kept in D-002 slice 1 with no deferral and no D-096 (A) grant. The blocker is the restored Linux pathless bind. Its ceremony is a genuine advance on the withdrawn IMA version — retained TCG2 log, TPM2_Quote with a nonce fixed to runIdentity and observedAt, AK verified against a certificate-store TCB member, quoted PCR 4 required to equal an event-log replay including the kernel event, and comprehensive fail-closed rules. But its central equality requires a PCR-4 EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION event digest to equal a package member's flat file sha-256, and those are different preimages: that event type carries the PE/COFF image digest computed with the checksum field, the certificate table entry and the attribute certificate region excluded. The artifact contains no handling of that distinction at all — zero occurrences of Authenticode, PE/COFF, PE image or image hash. So on a machine that satisfies every security property the ceremony proves, no payload member matches the event digest and the profile refuses. Because OS ABI must use PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED and may not be represented any other way, that leaves slice-1 Linux unqualifiable as a class — the exact condition Codex blocked at v25, now reached through a bind that is asserted LIVE rather than through a withdrawal. The fix is narrow: define the image-digest computation and compare against it, or bind through a measurement whose preimage is the file bytes. Everything else in the ceremony should be kept as written.
